title: How fast does a shot travel?
instruction: Estimate on the slider. Roughly is enough.
debrief: Every shot in an online game travels there and back through routers. Even light in a cable isn't infinitely fast. The further away the server, the higher the ping and the later you see the hit.

items.q: About how many kilometres does a signal in an optical cable travel in 1 millisecond (a thousandth of a second)?
items.why: Light in glass travels about 200,000 km a second, so 200 km a millisecond. Data can't travel faster than that.

items.q: The game server is 1,000 km away. How many milliseconds does the trip there and back take through the cable alone, without delays in routers?
items.why: There: 1,000 km in 5 ms, and back another 5 ms. The real ping is higher: the cable doesn't run straight and every router holds the packet up for a moment.

items.q: A server in Australia is about 16,000 km away. How many ms would the trip there and back take through the cable alone?
items.why: 32,000 km there and back divided by 200 km a millisecond is 160 ms. That’s why you play on a server that is close.

items.q: The game redraws the picture 60 times a second. How many milliseconds does one frame last?
items.why: 1,000 ms divided by 60 is about 16.7 ms. A ping of 200 ms is a delay of about 12 frames.
